subject: Every dumped coordinate over every fixture example: the line must exist in the input and the column must name a byte on it. Byte columns are counted from 1 on lines recognized from the complete source buffer.
purpose:
FIFTY-SEVEN ROWS IN ONE FAMILY, and that family is not owned by any step. It was 131 before 0a.6, 122 before 0a.12, 109 before D35, 106 before Step 10, 79 after Step 8.1, 69 after 8.3, 66 after 8.4 and 57 after Q44. Count from the data rather than from this paragraph, always: these family counts were already wrong by three once, and re-counting is what found it.

  57  end-at-line-ending              a coordinate names column 0 of a line that exists. There is no column 0; this is how "ends at the line ending" gets spelled when the only vocabulary is a coordinate. FIFTY-SEVEN are a block's end, H14's neighbour (section 11.4) -- and two of those joined this family at Step 9a.1 rather than being found there: they were `content-start-past-marker-line`, a footnote definition starting at the column AFTER its marker, which does not exist when the marker ends the line. The anchor rule made both starts places and left both ends where they were, so THE TOTAL DID NOT MOVE and the family did. A row here is one node, not one fault.
  --  recovered-table-cell IS GONE, and it is the one family this ledger closed by a RULING rather than a repair. Nine autocompleted table cells carried L:0..L:0, and column 0 is not a byte. Both coordinate spellings had been built and measured and both traded one wrongness for another, so it was carried as Q44 -- until the owner supplied the criterion that decides it on 2026-08-23: a scope is what a consumer follows to map a node back to the source, so a cell that completion invented points AT the place it was completed, which is the end of its row. It costs six sibling-overlap rows in specs/positions/containment.json, where they are registered with that reasoning. multi-line-span-ends-at-a-line-ending IS ALSO GONE, cleared by 8.4: a code span that crosses a line ending used to end at the line ending itself, because its extent stopped at the last byte of its CONTENT and that byte was a newline. Covering the backticks (Q45, the owner's ruling) makes the end the closing tick, which is a place. Three rows, and they were the last thing standing between this ledger and a two-family list. unmatched-code-span-literal AND escaped-byte-content-offset ARE ALSO GONE, cleared together by 8.3, AND THEY WERE ONE DEFECT WEARING TWO LABELS. Nine rows were filed under the first and one under the second; all ten were a text run whose literal begins or ends with a backtick, placed one column right, because an UNMATCHED backtick run took both its offsets from `subj->pos` -- one past the run -- instead of from the run's own bytes. Consolidation then carried that end onto the whole merged run: `` `hi`lo` `` reported Text 1:5..1:8 inside a seven-byte paragraph. One line. The `escaped-byte-content-offset` label was written at Step 10, on the row that survived the continuation-line family, and it was a guess that this file recorded as if it were a measurement -- it is not the escape class, it never was, and it went with the other nine. split-off-table-lead, continuation-line-content-offset, content-start-past-marker-line, multi-line-span and end-column-never-set went earlier; that is in the git history of this file rather than here, because the list of gone families cannot grow forever.

Three of the 69 are inline, out of 2,438 inline nodes; the gate prints that split on every run. It was thirty-seven of 2,275 before Step 10.

`class` is analysis and `closedBy` is measurement. A family whose owner is unassigned is one where the step that moves the rows proves the attribution by moving them, and this gate's CLEARED list is that proof. It has now gone both ways twice: Step 10 cleared the two families it was expected to and left one row inside one of them, and 8.3 cleared that row along with a family whose OWNER was right and whose stated CAUSE was not.

A coordinate on line zero is NOT counted here; scripts/audit-scope-sanity.mjs owns the 0:0..0:0 sentinel and the line-zero-with-a-column shape, and there is no line to measure a column against. A zero COLUMN on a real line is measurable and is counted. Where a row is both - Text 1:1..1:0 is a zero column AND a reversed range - the two ratchets interlock rather than overlap.

WHAT THIS ORACLE STILL CANNOT SEE, named at 0a.6 so it is not re-derived: a scope that is a place and is still wrong. Step 10 measured how large that blind spot is: of the forty golden rows it moved, this oracle could see twenty-one. Ten of the rest were well-formed columns taken from the wrong line origin - `aaa`, then thirteen spaces and `bbb`, reported the `bbb` at column 1 of a sixteen-byte line - and the statement that catches those is that the source bytes at a Text node's own scope must spell its own literal: 1,037 of 1,134 single-line verbatim literals agreed before Step 10, 1,069 after, 978 before 8.3 and 986 after, and not one that agreed has ever stopped agreeing.
